fields.meta_title: Interior Design Questionnaire for New Clients | Emergent
fields.meta_description: An interior design questionnaire that asks about each room and who lives there, then turns the answers into a plan. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an Interior Design Questionnaire That Drafts the Plan
fields.hero_description: Build an interior design questionnaire that collects photos room by room and saves every answer to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What the Questionnaire Settles Before the Visit
fields.features_subheading: Each section answers something you would otherwise ask on site, and the first visit starts from a draft plan, not a blank notepad.
fields.feature_1:
Only the rooms in the project

The client ticks the rooms in scope, and only those rooms bring their questions. A two-room refresh skips the kitchen, and a whole-home project walks through every room in order.
fields.feature_2:
Photos and measurements for each room

Each room asks for photos taken from the doorway, plus wall lengths and ceiling height. You see where the windows and outlets sit before the visit and can start a layout at a desk.
fields.feature_3:
Style chosen from pictures, not adjectives

A client who writes cozy might mean wool throws or dark paneled walls. The form shows pairs of room photos, asks which feels closer to home, and saves each pick with the answers.
fields.feature_4:
A budget split room by room

The client enters a total budget, then an amount for each room. The form adds the rooms as they type, and a plan with $46,000 across rooms and a $40,000 total shows its $6,000 gap.
fields.feature_5:
Each response saved and announced

Every questionnaire saves as a row in a database you own, with no response caps. The app emails you or posts in Slack when one arrives, with the client's name and budget up top.
fields.feature_6:
The full code, yours on a paid plan

On paid plans, export the questionnaire's full code and its database to your GitHub repository. A developer can then host it on your studio's site or connect it to the tools you use.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Projects Planned From the First Answers
fields.tab_content_1:
With two dogs and a child, 5 pieces need performance fabric

Hollowell Interiors designs family homes and asks who lives in each one. Its rule is performance fabric on every upholstered piece in a home with pets or a child under 6. Beatrix and Teodoro Sorrentino list two dogs and a 4-year-old. All 5 pieces planned for their family room arrive marked for it.
fields.tab_content_2:
Seven of 12 pieces go on the sourcing list

Brightling Design starts each project with what the client owns. Its questionnaire asks for a photo of every piece and one choice: keep or replace. Marisa Velasquez photographs 12 pieces and keeps 5, including a walnut dresser. Her sourcing list opens with 7 lines, each showing the piece it replaces.
fields.tab_content_3:
Of the 48 staff, 34 need a desk on the busiest day

Iveagh Workplace Studio fits out offices and asks each client for two numbers: total staff, and the most people in the office on any one day. Quennell Analytics has 48 staff and counts 34 in on Tuesdays, its busiest day. The first desk plan Iveagh drafts holds 34 desks instead of 48.
fields.tab_content_4:
To sleep 8, a king, a queen, and two bunk sets

Hemi Ngata wants Gullrock Cottage to sleep 8 guests in 3 bedrooms. His designer's rental questionnaire asks for both numbers first. They set the bed plan before any style question: a king in the main bedroom, a queen in the second, and two sets of twin bunks in the third.

fields.howto_title: How to Make an Interior Design Questionnaire
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to turn what you ask on a first visit into an interior design questionnaire, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what the answers must settle
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Give every room its own section
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Note the answers that change a plan
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the decisions you want made before the first visit: which rooms are in scope, who uses them, what furniture stays, and the budget. Every question should feed one of those decisions. A question that feeds none can wait for the consultation.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open with whole-home questions such as the household and the total budget. Then give each room the same core set: how it is used and what bothers the client about it today, plus doorway photos and wall measurements.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Read three past projects and note each answer that changed what you specified, like a dog that meant tougher fabric or a home office that needed a door. Each one becomes a rule the questionnaire marks on the response, instead of something you remember.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Choose 6 pairs of room photos that differ on one thing at a time: warm or cool wood, pattern or plain fabric, and full shelves or bare ones. Each pick lands on the response next to the room it applies to.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write the prompt the way you would brief an assistant: the sections, the room list, the rules from step 3, and the photo pairs. Emergent builds the questionnaire and its database from that prompt, and you change any part by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Fill it in as last year's client
fields.howto_step_6_des: Answer the questionnaire as a client from a finished project, using what they told you at the time. Check that every rule marks what you would have decided, and that the response reads in the order you plan a project.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Send it the day an inquiry arrives
fields.howto_step_7_des: Reply to each new inquiry with the questionnaire link and a date to finish it, a few days before the consultation. You then walk into the first meeting with the client's photos and a draft plan already in hand.

faq_plan.q: What is an interior design questionnaire?
faq_plan.a: An interior design questionnaire is the set of questions a designer sends a new client before the first consultation. It asks who lives in the home, which rooms are in the project, what furniture stays, the client's style, the budget, and the timeline. The answers become the designer's starting brief before anyone visits.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an interior design questionnaire?
faq_plan.a: Start with the decisions the answers must settle, then group the questions by room. Describe that structure to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English, including the photo uploads and any rule, such as marking fabric for homes with pets. It builds the form and a database for the answers. Try it with a past client's details before the first real send.

faq_plan.q: What should an interior design questionnaire template include?
faq_plan.a: Five parts: contact details and the property address, the household with pets and children's ages, the rooms in scope with photos, the furniture that stays, and the budget with a target finish date. Put style questions after the practical ones. If you start from an interior design questionnaire PDF, keep its sections but move them into a form where each photo arrives filed under its room.

faq_plan.q: What should a commercial interior design questionnaire ask about the client's brand?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the logo, the brand colors with their codes, the typefaces, and three words the space should feel like to a visitor. In a shop or a restaurant, those answers steer the finishes and the signage. If the client is still working out the brand itself, send a brand questionnaire first and design the space once it is settled.

faq_plan.q: How do I ask about budget in an interior design questionnaire?
faq_plan.a: Ask for one total, then ask what it covers: furniture and decor only, or the construction work as well. Two clients who both write $40,000 can be describing two different projects until that line is answered. Ask whether the figure is firm or a starting point, and save the per-room split for later in the form.

faq_plan.q: How long should an interior design questionnaire be?
faq_plan.a: Keep it short enough to finish in one sitting; about 25 questions plus photos is a workable ceiling. Leave anything you learn faster in person, such as how a fabric feels or how loud a room is, for the consultation. Emergent builds the form from a prompt, and cutting a section later is a one-line change to that prompt.

faq_plan.q: When should a client fill out an interior design questionnaire?
faq_plan.a: Before the first consultation. Reading the answers first lets the consultation start from the client's photos and budget instead of a blank page. After the client signs, a client onboarding questionnaire collects what the job itself needs, such as access instructions and who approves invoices.

faq_plan.q: What should an office interior design questionnaire ask clients?
faq_plan.a: Ask how the office is used, not only how big the team is. Beyond total staff and the busiest-day count, ask which teams sit together and how many meeting rooms are booked at peak. Then ask where people take calls and how much the headcount should grow during the lease. The app Emergent builds can send each response to any project tool with an API.

faq_plan.q: Can clients upload room photos and measurements in an interior design questionnaire?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Each room section can take photos and wall measurements, and the uploads save with that room's answers. Ask for daylight photos from the doorway and one straight-on shot of each window wall, with the window width noted. A questionnaire built with Emergent has no response caps, which matters in the months when inquiries pile up.

faq_plan.q: Should a one-room refresh get the same interior design questionnaire as a full home?
faq_plan.a: No. A full-home questionnaire asks far more than a single-room job needs. For one-off work such as a bedroom refresh or styling a bookshelf wall, a short project request form with photos of the room and a budget gives you enough to quote.
